item.title: AirLink 0.10.0
item.description:
AirLink 0.10.0 makes adding trusted computers and keeping the transfer list tidy easier. This is a private development preview for manual download and installation.
## Device connection
- **Add a device** starts with nearby computers. Choose a computer, compare its complete fingerprint with **This device** on the other computer, then approve the connection there once. Manual address entry remains available. - **This device** shows the computer name, HTTPS address and grouped fingerprint first. Browser certificate/QR setup is a separate path for phones and tablets. - Trusted devices and their settings are easier to find. **Automatically receive from this device** is directly available for the selected paired device, and remains an explicit local choice. Each receiving computer controls its own permission.
## A tidy transfer list
- **Remove from list** removes one completed, failed or cancelled file-transfer entry. - **Remove finished entries…** asks for confirmation and removes only the entries captured when selected. Active transfers and transfers finishing later stay visible. - Removal is persistent. Originals, received files and independent Quick Share sources remain available. Lifetime payload counters remain separate from history-derived totals. - Older status responses cannot restore removed entries or stale device settings.
## Install manually
Download the universal macOS DMG or Windows x64/ARM64 Setup below. For Intel/AMD Windows, choose the x64 Setup. Quit the existing app before replacing it or when Setup asks. Keep only the intended current AirLink app in `/Applications`; settings, pairings and received files remain separate.
The repository is private during development. Sign in to GitHub with repository access to download a build. The existing unauthenticated in-app updater cannot access this private feed/download channel.
## Verification and limits
Completed background checks: **174 top-level Go race tests / 287 cases**, `go vet`, **63 Swift tests** including actual two-service transfer/removal/restart verification, **37 Windows Core tests** against the final service, and **68 web tests**. Universal macOS and both native Windows architecture builds passed. No app GUI, Windows installer or browser UI was automated; physical Windows interaction and real-network acceptance remain separate.
macOS remains ad hoc signed and not notarized; Windows Setup has no Authenticode signature. Ed25519 package/feed signatures provide a separate authenticity check. Package checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Linux stays experimental and source-only with no binary download. No new 100 GiB or WLAN throughput result is claimed.
